 Kyrie Irving 
 DAL

 Kyrie Irving (knee) is off the injury report for Wednesday’s game against the Spurs. 
 Irving did not play in Monday’s loss to the Kings, with Caleb Martin replacing him in the starting lineup. With Max Christie (hip) out, Martin could stay in the starting five even after Irving’s return. 
 Caleb Martin 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #16 
 Cooper Flagg, Max Christie, Caleb Martin, PJ Washington and Daniel Gafford will start Monday’s game against the Kings. 
 The Mavericks won’t have Kyrie Irving for Monday’s game, which opens a spot in the starting lineup. Martin will fill the void, which raises his fantasy ceiling. However, that isn’t enough to make him a worthwhile streamer in most leagues, since there are 15 games on Monday’s schedule. 
 Naji Marshall 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #3 
 Naji Marshall (illness) is now probable for Friday’s game against the Rockets. 
 Initially questionable for Friday’s game, Marshall is on track to return after a two-game absence. Marcus Sasser (22 minutes), Walter Clayton Jr. (15 minutes), and Caleb Martin (14 minutes) all played rotation minutes in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder. Their playing time may decrease if Marshall is cleared to play. 
 Naji Marshall 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #3 
 Naji Marshall (illness) is questionable to play against the Rockets on Friday. 
 Marshall has missed the Mavs’ last two games with an illness and is in danger of missing a third. In that scenario, Marcus Sasser, Walter Clayton Jr. and Caleb Martin would all continue to take on a few extra minutes off the bench. 
 Caleb Martin 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #16 
 Caleb Martin (thumb) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Thunder. 
 Martin will be available to make his season debut on Wednesday after missing time with a sprained right thumb. While he may slide into the Mavericks’ rotation, Martin isn’t worth rostering in redraft leagues. 
 Caleb Martin 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #16 
 Caleb Martin (thumb) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Thunder. 
 Martin hasn’t appeared in a game this season yet. However, if he is available on Wednesday, the Mavericks’ many injuries could thrust him into the rotation immediately. That wouldn’t be enough to make Martin a player worth rostering in fantasy leagues. 
 Caleb Martin 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #16 
 Caleb Martin (thumb) is out for Monday’s game against the Heat. 
 No surprise here unfortunately as Martin is yet to appear in a game this season thanks to a sprained right thumb. His continued absence doesn’t impact fantasy basketball, however. 
 Caleb Martin 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #16 
 Caleb Martin (thumb) is doubtful for Monday’s game against the Heat. 
 Dealing with a sprained right thumb, Martin has yet to appear in a game this season, and that appears unlikely to change on Monday. If he sits, Martin’s continued absence won’t impact fantasy basketball. 
 Cooper Flagg 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #32 
 Cooper Flagg (shoulder) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Heat. 
 Flagg being listed as questionable on the Mavericks’ initial injury report is good news for fantasy managers. After he sustained a shoulder injury during Friday’s win over the Pacers, expectations were that the reigning Rookie of the Year would miss a few days. Now, Flagg could miss just one game after sitting out Saturday’s loss to the Spurs. If he returns, Zaccharie Risacher will head to the bench. 
 Zaccharie Risacher 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #10 
 Zaccharie Risacher recorded 11 points (4-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, two assists, one steal, two blocks and one three-pointer in Saturday’s loss to the Spurs. 
 After Cooper Flagg sustained a left shoulder injury in Friday’s win over the Pacers, Risacher started for the Mavericks for the first time on Saturday. He had a highlight-worthy block on Victor Wembanyama at the rim in the first half, but his overall production wasn’t enough to put Risacher on the streaming radar. Naji Marshall and PJ Washington (12 points, four rebounds and two assists) are better fantasy options until Flagg returns.

 Victor Wembanyama finished Wednesday’s win over the Mavericks with 52 points (16-of-28 FGs, 19-of-23 FTs), 24 rebounds, two assists, two steals, eight blocks and one three-pointer.
 The Mavericks aren’t the first team to have no answer for Wembanyama, and they certainly won’t be the last. He was dominant throughout, becoming the second player in league history to finish a game with at least 50 points, 20 rebounds and five blocks since the NBA began recording blocks as an official stat. The other player: Bob McAdoo in 1974. Wembanyama’s 52 points are a new career high, and he shot 1-of-8 from beyond the arc. Just an incredible showing from one of the NBA’s elite talents. Wembanyama appeared to tweak his right ankle in the fourth quarter, but he did not receive medical attention while on the bench and returned for crunch time.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Following Wednesday’s win over the Suns, Trail Blazers head coach Micah Nori said that Vit Krejčí (leg) suffered a fracture. 
 Krejčí exited Wednesday’s game with what the Trail Blazers described as a left ankle injury. Unfortunately, based on Nori’s update, he’s likely to be out for the foreseeable future. Krejčí’s absence won’t significantly affect fantasy basketball, but it does leave Portland down another wing option with Shaedon Sharpe already out.

 Devin Booker had 33 points (9-of-19 FGs, 13-of-13 FTs), one rebound, two assists and two three-pointers against the Trail Blazers on Wednesday. 
 Booker was just 2-of-8 from behind the three-point line in this one, but made his hay at the foul line as he drained all 13 of his free throw attempts on his way to a 33-point game. The 30-year-old guard played almost 34 minutes despite fouling out for the second consecutive game. Booker and the Suns will be back on the floor Thursday at home against the Magic. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Reed Sheppard finished Wednesday’s loss to the Timberwolves with 14 points (5-of-12 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), two rebounds, two assists, three steals and three three-pointers.
 Sheppard has now scored in double figures in three of the six games he’s played this season. Against the Timberwolves, his final stat line included a season-high three steals. With the Rockets signing Marcus Smart (four points, one rebound, one assist, one block and one three-pointer) during the offseason and Fred VanVleet back from a torn ACL, Sheppard’s upside in redraft leagues is limited as long as both veterans are healthy. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Donovan Clingan had 24 points (9-of-12 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), 11 rebounds, one assist, one steal, three blocks and one three-pointer against the Suns on Wednesday. 
 Clingan has posted back-to-back dominant performances that have led to double-doubles in his last two games. He had 24 points on 12 attempts, one three-pointer and a full stat line against the Suns Wednesday. We’ll see if Clingan can keep up this production in tougher matchups against the Lakers and Spurs this weekend.

 Fred VanVleet amassed 18 points (6-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, three assists and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
 Back in the Rockets’ lineup after sitting out Monday’s win over the Celtics, VanVleet played 30 minutes against the Timberwolves. Even though he shot 50 percent from the field on Wednesday, the Rockets’ guard is making just 39 percent of his attempts this season. VanVleet has long offered little value in that category. But most fantasy managers know he’ll do enough across the board to be a solid category-league option. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 RJ Barrett put up 22 points (7-of-17 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, and three 3-pointers in 128-109 loss to the Nuggets.
 Barrett led the team in shot attempts in this game and he did a good job scoring the ball. On the season, he’s averaging 20.9 points, 6 rebounds, 3.9 assists, 0.5 steals, and 0.5 blocks, shooting 48.1% from the field, 59.5% from the free throw line, and 31.8% from three. Outside of the free throw percentage, he’s been great for where he was selected in redraft leagues. There’s even room for him to get better once he starts hitting more of his free throws.

 Şengün, who has recorded three double-doubles this season, notched his first triple-double on Wednesday. He didn’t shoot the ball well, but the Rockets center is shooting 54.1 percent from the field this season. This has been an encouraging start for Şengün, whether you’re talking category or points leagues.

 Damian Lillard had 25 points (9-of-17 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, five assists and two three-pointers in the Trail Blazers’ 132-119 victory over the Suns on Wednesday. 
 Lillard has now scored 25 points and had at least five assists in both of his matchups against the Suns so far this season. The 36-year-old point guard played 32 minutes and was +16 in the 13-point win. Portland begins a back-to-back against the Lakers and Spurs Friday in Los Angeles.
